payload.title: Registration/runtime diagnosis (docs-sourced)

question_a_stale_registrations.finding: Revoking authorization and removing registration are separate layers. Revoking auth is server-side; the local registration persists.
documented_removal_paths: Settings > Computer Use > Always allow: remove apps to revoke saved decisions (official docs).
codex mcp remove computer-use: removes manual MCP server registration.
Native host manifest: separate local file, must be removed independently.
$CODEX_HOME/config.toml [computer_use.windows] always_allowed_app_ids: Windows persistent decisions live here.
question_a_stale_registrations.why_stale: If only server-side auth was revoked, the local MCP registration, native host manifest, and always-allow entries remain. They show as 'registered' because they are — locally.

question_b_missing_node_repl.finding: node_repl is host-exposed, not plugin-bundled. The skill loads via marketplace discovery; the tool lives on the host.
question_b_missing_node_repl.explanation: Official docs: 'Files, credentials, permissions, plugins, browser setup, Computer Use, and local tools stay on the connected host.' A delegated session runs in a different host context without the native host tools installed. Your local desktop task works because that host has the native host registered. The delegated session's host does not.
question_b_missing_node_repl.why_skill_loads: Plugin/skill discovery goes through the marketplace cache, which is shared or synced. Host tool availability is per-machine.

duplicate_registration_test.confirm: Run 'codex mcp list' — two computer-use entries (one plugin-owned, one manual) confirms duplication.
duplicate_registration_test.falsify: Single entry means no duplication; the issue is elsewhere (stale marketplace cache or native host manifest).
duplicate_registration_test.documented_fix: Remove the stale manual MCP registration so it does not compete with the plugin-owned registration (issue #33248 recovery step 6).

polling_interval.route: cron worker -> git ls-remote -> fetch on change
